 By Iris Samuels Updated: 46 minutes ago Published: 47 minutes ago Democratic gubernatorial candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins enters The Broken Blender for an election night party in downtown Anchorage on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. (Bill Roth / ADN) Democrat Mary Peltola extended her lead over Republican U.S. Sen. Dan S. Sullivan in Alaska’s Senate race after the state Division of Elections tallied an additional 5,000 ballots on Thursday, bringing the total number of ballots counted to over 256,000. 
 In the governor’s race, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins had over 50% of first-choice votes after the latest ballot count , ahead of three Republican candidates. Kreiss-Tomkins said Wednesday that he expects that after all ballots are counted, he will have a comfortable majority of votes on his way to becoming the state’s first Democratic governor since 2002. 
 Thousands of absentee ballots remain to be counted in Alaska, with final ballot counting scheduled to take place Nov. 18. 
 Many of the ballots counted Thursday came from Juneau and surrounding areas in Southeast Alaska, which favored Peltola and Kreiss-Tomkins in their respective races.
 Among the three Republicans in the governor’s race, Bernadette Wilson has 28.7% of first-choice votes; Dave Bronson has 13.7%; and Treg Taylor has 7.3%.
 [ Kreiss-Tomkins previews policy priorities as he awaits final election results ] 
 In the Senate race, Peltola is on track to become the latest Democrat to flip a U.S. Senate seat previously held by a Republican. After Thursday’s ballot count, she had 49.1% of first-choice votes, ahead of Sullivan’s 46.8%.
 ADVERTISEMENT Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate Mary Peltola and Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan. (Marc Lester and Anne Raup / ADN) Peltola, a former U.S. representative, saw her lead grow to 5,800 votes, about 1,825 votes more than her lead on Wednesday.
 If the top vote-getter in the ranked-choice election receives less than 50% of first-choice votes, the result will be determined by ranked choice tabulation.
 The remaining candidates on the Senate ballot are Gerald Heikes, a Republican perennial candidate from Palmer who has 2.1% of first-choice votes, and Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg who has 1.6% of first-choice votes.
 If the incumbent Sullivan was ranked by enough of Heikes’ and the Petersburg Sullivan’s voters, he could overtake Peltola. However, preliminary data indicates that Peltola would remain ahead of Sullivan even after a ranked choice tabulation.
 ADVERTISEMENT In the race for Alaska’s lone U.S. House seat, Republican incumbent Rep. Nick Begich is comfortably ahead with 48.5% of first-choice votes. Independent challenger Bill Hill has 41.1%. Eric Hafner, a New York felon running as a Democrat, has 7.5%. Libertarian Jim McDermott has 2.6%. 
 Independent candidate Bill Hill (left) and Republican incumbent U.S. Rep. Nick Begich (right). (Marc Lester and Bill Roth / ADN) A ballot measure seeking to repeal Alaska’s election system has failed to pass, with 52.8% of voters against it. The measure had been backed by the Alaska Republican Party. 
 A separate measure affirming an existing requirement that Alaska voters be U.S. citizens is on track to pass with 68.9% voting in favor of it.
 Several state legislative races remain too close to call as ballot counting continues. However, results so far indicate that Democrat-dominated bipartisan majorities will continue to control both the Alaska House and Senate. 
 2026 Alaska state elections Iris Samuels
 Iris Samuels is a reporter for the Anchorage Daily News focusing on state politics. She previously covered Montana for The AP and Report for America and wrote for the Kodiak Daily Mirror. Contact her at isamuels@adn.com.
